title: The Locker of the water tower
premise: Quentin Eastwick, a scholarship transfer student at Hollowmere Academy, plans to survive senior year by being forgettable—until the college essay prompt 'What have you lost that no one else knows about?' cracks the school open. He discovers a rusted locker in the base of the old water tower, sealed since 1997, holding evidence of a student who vanished and was quietly erased. As Quentin and three unlikely allies dig into what the school's founding families buried, they learn justice at Hollowmere has always been administered off the books. At prom, Quentin trades his invisibility for testimony, exposing the cover-up and accepting expulsion rather than silence—and finds, for the first time, that belonging is something you claim, not something you're granted.
about_author: Rosalind Amberdale is a former boarding school archivist who spent years cataloguing the things institutions prefer forgotten. She writes young adult fiction about teenagers who refuse to be footnotes.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Unremarkable
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Establishes his survival rules at Hollowmere: sit near exits, never volunteer, count days. A guidance counselor hands him the Common App essay prompt as an assignment, and he dismisses it. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, the loneliness inside his strategy.

chapters.title: The Question on Page One
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In English class, students read their draft essays aloud; each confession lands like a small detonation in the room. Quentin writes nothing, but the prompt lodges in him. Beat: discomfort awakening—the first crack in his armor.

chapters.title: Detour Past the Tower
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Cutting across the maintenance yard to avoid bullies, he notices the decommissioned water tower and a rusted padlock on a hatch no one maintains. Beat: curiosity he can't unfeel.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows Things
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The school's unofficial historian—a lunch lady's daughter with keys to everything—catches Quentin sketching the tower. She warns him off, which tells him there's something to warn him off from. Beat: wary alliance forming.

chapters.title: What the Lock Kept
chapters.summary: Quentin and Marisol's POV alternating. They open the hatch and find Locker 114, welded shut, stenciled with a name: D. Okafor, 1997. Inside: letters, a broken watch stopped at 11:47, and a disciplinary file stamped EXPUNGED. Beat: dread and thrill.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Was Never Here
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Yearbooks show Daniel Okafor photographed in September 1996 and airbrushed from every page after. The library's copies of the school paper are razor-cut. Beat: horror at how thoroughly a person can be deleted.

chapters.title: Three Is a Conspiracy
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, a legacy student and Quentin's lab partner, catches them with the file—and instead of reporting it, admits his grandfather signed the expulsion order. Beat: guilt-driven defection; the circle widens.

chapters.title: Rules of the Unwritten Court
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She explains Hollowmere's tradition of 'quiet resolutions'—problems handled by the Founders' Council, never the police. Daniel's sister once protested and was paid to disappear too. Beat: anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Watch Stopped at 11:47
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Research reveals Daniel was last seen the night before a fire in the tower's pump house—an accident officially, though the fire report is missing. Beat: the stakes shift from mystery to possible death.

chapters.title: Someone Else Has Been Looking
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They find fresh scratches on the locker and a note in Daniel's handwriting style: 'If you found this, don't trust the ones who smile.' Someone is watching them. Beat: paranoia; the hunter becomes hunted.

chapters.title: Midterm Silence
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Headmaster Voss invites Quentin to tea, offers him a full-ride recommendation letter, and mentions his scholarship is 'renewable by discretion.' The message is unmistakable. Beat: temptation and fear—the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Took the Money
chapters.summary: Grace Okafor's POV (a chapter-length letter/interview). Now a nurse two states away, she explains why she accepted the settlement: she had nothing, and grief doesn't pay rent. Beat: devastating empathy; the cost of losing without power.

chapters.title: Everything We Were Going to Be
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Reading Daniel's unsent letters—college applications, a poem, a plan to be the first in his family to graduate—Quentin sees himself. He drafts his essay for real, telling the truth. Beat: identification; invisibility becomes unbearable.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The tower hatch is padlocked again and the locker contents gone—someone got there first. Marisol's mother is reassigned suddenly. Beat: the institution strikes back; despair.

chapters.title: The Backup Nobody Thought Teenagers Would Make
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Reveal: she photographed and scanned everything weeks ago, and Grace kept Daniel's original letters. But going public means expulsion for all three and legal exposure. Beat: resolve crystallizing into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Stage
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The trio learns the Founders' Council attends prom to present the Voss Scholarship. They decide to act there, where witnesses can't be quietly dismissed. Beat: grim determination; the trap set in reverse.

chapters.title: Eleven Forty-Seven
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Quentin's POV. During the scholarship presentation, Quentin takes the microphone and reads Daniel's final letter aloud as the gymnasium lights flicker—Voss cuts power, but phones are already recording. Beat: terror transfigured into voice.

chapters.title: The Room Where It Was Decided
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Theo's POV. Theo confronts his grandfather publicly with the expunged file; the council fractures, one member confessing on record. Police—who were never called in 1997—finally are. Beat: justice arriving loud and messy.

chapters.title: Expelled, and Lighter
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin is expelled for the disruption; Marisol and Theo face hearings. Walking out past the water tower, he feels no defeat. His essay—'What I lost was my silence'—is submitted anyway. Beat: costly victory, identity claimed.

chapters.title: The Name Back on the Wall
chapters.summary: Grace's POV. Weeks later, the school installs a memorial plaque; Daniel's name returns to the yearbook reprint. It isn't enough—it never will be—but it's true. Beat: imperfect restitution honored.

chapters.title: Acceptance Letter
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Another college, reading his essay, accepts him and offers aid—not charity this time, but recognition. He packs one box; it's lighter than when he arrived. Beat: earned hope; belonging redefined.

chapters.title: The Locker of the Water Tower
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Quentin's POV, one year later. He returns for Grace's dedication of a scholarship in Daniel's name, and the new lock on the hatch is ceremonial—opened, not sealed. He answers a freshman's question about the story with the truth. Beat: closure; the question nobody can stop answering finally answered honestly.
